articles.title: 'A tricky one': Dravid reveals big concern over Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's Test future
articles.description: The year 2026 has been particularly memorable for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. He ended the IPL season as Rajasthan Royals' highest run-scorer with 776 runs. He then produced another explosive performance, smashing 94 off 29 balls against Sri Lanka 'A' in the List A tri-series final in Colombo. He made his senior India debut against England in July and followed it up with an impressive tour of Zimbabwe. Sooryavanshi finished the series with 151 runs, the most by any batter, and was named Player of the Series. He has scored 193 runs in six T20I innings at a strike rate of 189.21.

articles.description: Eddie Owens Martin, an innovative and unconventional artist, dedicated nearly three decades to transforming his land in Georgia into the vibrant, visionary art space known as Pasaquan. He intricately combined various cultural elements through his painted totems and impressive masonry. After years of exposure and deterioration, the Kohler Foundation intervened with a major restoration, breathing new life into this unique site.

articles.title: 'Awarapan 2' box office collection day 12: Inches towards Rs 150 cr, to face competition from Toxic
Toxic Movie Review and Release Live Updates
articles.full_text: With the worldwide release scheduled for August 26, attention will now shift to the film's first reviews, audience reactions and box office performance. For Yash, the release represents an important return after the enormous success of 'KGF: Chapter 2'. For Geetu Mohandas, it marks a major opportunity to present a large-scale gangster drama to a global audience. The movie is set against the backdrop of post-independence Goa. It follows a gangster caught between violence, loyalty, ambition and personal conflicts. The story explores the consequences of choices made in a world where relationships and power often overlap. The strong pre-sales have placed 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' in a favourable position before its first show. Its India advance booking had already reached Rs 43.64 crore by Tuesday afternoon. The reported Rs 70 crore-plus global advance sales further strengthen expectations. The final Day 1 figure will depend on additional bookings and occupancy across markets and also the WOM matters/ Yash plays two characters in 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups'. He portrays Raya and his son Rumi, who is also known as Ticket. The father-son relationship is expected to form an important part of the story. Their connection places family, identity and power at the centre of the gangster narrative. 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' will release worldwide on August 26. The movie is expected to open across multiple markets and languages. The combination of Yash's return, a reported Rs 500 crore budget, an extensive cast and strong advance bookings has created major expectations around its opening. 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' has been mounted on a reported budget of around Rs 500 crore. The reported scale makes it one of the most expensive Indian productions. The movie combines gangster drama with action and psychological themes. Its production design and large-scale action sequences have been major points of discussion during the promotional campaign. Yash has described the film as an ambitious project that goes beyond conventional commercial cinema. Speaking at a promotional event at Malla Reddy University in Hyderabad, the actor discussed the film's themes and creative approach. “Toxic is bold. Toxic is original. Toxic is ambitious. Toxic is path-breaking. Toxic will blow your mind. Beyond that, it’s a movie that is very deep. Psychologically, what I believe is, art should always push you to the darkest corners and make you ask those uncomfortable questions about human relationships and what we go through psychologically in life. So it’s a great film which will speak to you on a personal level also.” According to Venky Box Office, the movie had grossed $292,541 across 362 locations and 873 shows in the UK. The overseas numbers have added another positive factor to the film's opening prospects. The movie has also made an impact in the UK before its theatrical release. 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' has reportedly secured more than 400 screens in the territory. The scale is being described as unprecedented for a Kannada film in the market. It also underlines the reach Yash has developed following the success of the 'KGF' movies. 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' marks Yash's first major theatrical release since the 'KGF' franchise. The actor's return has generated considerable interest among audiences across different markets. The film is arriving 503 days after its initially announced release date of April 10, 2025. Production delays resulted in several changes to the release schedule before the makers finally announced August 26 as the theatrical date. The film's pre-release momentum extends beyond India. Advance sales across markets have reportedly crossed the Rs 70 crore mark. The numbers indicate strong interest in Yash's return to theatres. The movie is also expected to benefit from its release across multiple language markets. The movie has already registered an impressive response through advance ticket sales. According to Sacnilk, 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' had recorded a Day 1 advance booking gross of Rs 43.64 crore in India as of 1 pm on August 25. The figure includes block seats. With the release still ahead, the advance sales could increase further before the first shows begin. The Telugu market has emerged as another strong contributor to the film's pre-release business. According to the available figures, 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' has recorded around Rs 15 crore in gross pre-sales in the Telugu market. The response adds to the film's prospects ahead of its worldwide opening.
